subject: SDK: intermittent model variant fallback in streaming - repro + roadmap ask
messages:
From: James Holloway <james.h@orbitalhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Orbital Health Platform <platform@orbitalhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Strange streaming behavior when variantRouting enabled (production)

Hi Karthik,

Quick heads-up: we started seeing inconsistent outputs yesterday evening from our production integration using the Java SDK (v1.3.2) when the client has variantRouting enabled. About 3% of requests during a 30m window returned a different model (we saw a fallback to lightweight-model-v2) mid-stream — which caused truncated JSON outputs and one notable hallucination that surfaced in our UI.

I attached a minimal repro (repro_steps.txt) and a short screencap of the session (repro_screencap.mp4). We believe the client requested model "redwood-xl-1" with streaming=true and routingHints set to prefer region-us-west, but the trace shows a switch to lightweight-model-v2 after the first 120 tokens.

This is impacting a small segment of our users (not all sessions) but is high visibility for us. Can you advise next steps or open an internal ticket? We need either a short-term mitigation (turn off variantRouting on our side?) or a fast patch if this looks like a server/runtime race.

Thanks,
James
Director, Platform Engineering
Orbital Health

Attachments: repro_steps.txt, repro_screencap.mp4

James — thanks for the quick report and the repro artifacts. Looping in Dev (runtime) and Stephanie (sales-eng) so we can triage and coordinate with Orbital.

Immediate asks:
- Dev: can you confirm whether routing decisions can change mid-stream or whether this looks like an aggressive fallback being applied after the initial token?
- Dev / Product (Marissa): if this is an expected behavior for cost-tier fallbacks, we need a clear SDK-level toggle customers can use to opt into a "stable-route" mode for critical flows. Orbital is asking for a short-term mitigation while we investigate.
- Stephanie: I copied MAP-OrbitalHealth.xlsx to track the MAP items and timeline — please work the customer for expectations.

James — we'll keep you posted within the next 24 hours.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Strange streaming behavior when variantRouting enabled (production)

Thanks for the signal and the repro, James. I pulled the minimal repro and a few initial notes below. I've opened INF-4821 with the logs we already have.

Repro summary (what I ran):
- Java SDK v1.3.2, streaming=true, model=redwood-xl-1, variantRouting=ON, routingHints: {region: us-west, costTier: standard}
- Sent a 512-token prompt; observed server ACK for redwood-xl-1 but after ~120 tokens the session switched to lightweight-model-v2 and stream contained mismatched tokens (JSON schema mismatch)

Initial hypothesis:
- There's a race between routing decision and session-level KV cache population when autoscaling triggers a fallback path. If a fallback is applied mid-stream, the runtime resumes on a compatible model but with different tokenizer/sequence semantics causing token boundary mismatches.
- SDK currently allows server-initiated fallback without an explicit SDK-level signal to app code. That makes it hard for customers to decide whether to retry or abort.

Immediate mitigations we can try (short-term):
1) Server: block mid-stream model switches for sessions with streaming=true for the next 24–48h for affected customers (requesting a feature flag).
2) SDK: add a quick opt-in flag --stableRoute=true (server-validated) so the server won't apply mid-stream fallback for sessions that request stability.
3) Telemetry: add a per-request header and metric (X-Route-Change: true/false) to record if a route change happened during the session so we can measure impact.

I can prototype (2) as a small SDK change and produce a patch build by EOD tomorrow. Need Product confirmation on API semantics and a quick canary rollout strategy.

INF-4821: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4821
Logs attached: runtime_routing_snippet.log (snippet) — full logs saved to incident bucket.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: SDK stable-route proposal + MAP for Orbital Health (customer impact)

Team — forwarding the triage notes. Orbital is a strategic POC: they are in pilot, but this issue touches their clinical ingestion flows and the customer has asked for an SLA clarity. We need a two-track approach: short-term mitigation (no mid-stream switches) + near-term SDK opt-in.

Proposed customer-facing plan (for MAP-OrbitalHealth.xlsx):
- 24h: apply server-side feature flag to block mid-stream model switches for pilot tenants (Risk: slightly higher cost under pressure).
- 72h: release SDK patch (stableRoute flag) and share patch build with Orbital for quick verification.
- 2 weeks: product/engineering decide on the longer-term behavior (default off vs on, metrics gating, rollout).

Ask to Product (Marissa): prioritization as P1 for pilot/dedicated customers on this deal. Ask to Dev: estimate for SDK patch + server flag (canary + rollback strategy).

James — attaching the MAP sheet with proposed timeline and who owns what. We'll keep you posted and aim for the server short-term toggle by EOD today if we get approvals.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP-OrbitalHealth.xlsx

Thanks everyone for the clear triage notes and proposed mitigations. I agree with the two-track approach. Product decision and next steps: 

1) Prioritization: marking this P1 for pilot / dedicated customers (Orbital included). We will fund the short-term server toggle and the SDK opt-in patch.
2) API contract: Dev, please propose the SDK flag name (I like "stableRoute") and whether it should be a boolean request field or a config on the SDK client. We'll treat it as an explicit opt-in for now.
3) Rollout: implement server-side feature flag that suppresses mid-stream model switches for sessions with streaming=true or stableRoute=true. Can we get a canary by EOD (Dev) limited to a single region and to a specific tenancy tag?
4) Telemetry: add X-Route-Change metric to the request trace so we can report incidence rate by customer in Console (Marissa -> Observability team follow-up).

Dev: please provide an engineering estimate (hours + risk) by COB Monday. Stephanie / Karthik: please keep Orbital updated with the timeline we discussed.

Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference
